answer: To register a node, an agent must stake a bond that is escrowed and slashed if one identity spawns many accounts. Identity proofs are chained like a trellis, each linked to verified prior work, so a Sybil farm cannot mint a fresh uncorrelated key for free. Every extra account also pays a per-epoch fee that must cross a river of real compute, not bookkeeping entries. Newcomers start behind a lantern check: a seasoned peer co-signs and shares liability, so forging a cluster requires real collateral per identity. Cost scales each fake account, turning a cheap flood expensive.
